text.p: Tropical cyclone Gretelle is making landfall along the southeast coast of Madagascar. Top winds are estimated at 130 mph. Winds damage at coastal areas is likely quite high. It is also likely that a major storm surge is causing coastal flooding and considerable damage...especially north of the track. Winds weaken some as the system moves inland however they will still be strong enough to cause considerable damage. Rains of at least 7-15 inches will lead to massive flooding and severe mudslides as this system tracks inland. Damage should become extreme, especially due to flooding and mudslides.

Tropical Cyclone Pancho-Helinda, with 105 mph winds, is near 15s/89e in the southern Indian Ocean, moving southwest at 3 mph. Slow weakening will continue but this storm will continue to be a significant threat to shipping this period.

Tropical Cyclone Iletta, with 45 mph winds, is near 15s/65e in the southern Indian Ocean, moving southwest at 5 mph. Slow strengthening is expected making the storm more of a threat to shipping during the next couple days.
There are no further statements at this time.
